tasks.short: Meet with the kindergarten team and management, gather evaluation data on the programme, draft revisions, check them with the team, and share the revised programme with staff.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher collaborates with other teachers and administrators on the kindergarten program in team meetings
Kindergarten teacher gathers evaluation data on the programme from class records
Kindergarten teacher drafts revisions to the programme document

loop.input: The team's agreed changes, the evaluation data and the current programme text.
loop.output: A draft revised programme text with objectives per theme.
loop.check: Code checks every objective maps to a core goal code from the fixed list; the teacher then reads the draft against the team's agreed changes and the evaluation data and removes or rewrites text that says more or other than was agreed.
loop.stop: Stops when every objective maps and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Programme text must explain the changes in prose; a template only holds the goal list.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher checks the revised programme with the team: each change says what the team agreed and fits the evaluation data
Kindergarten teacher publishes the checked programme to staff: by e-mail today, on the school's shared page after the change

tasks.design: Group overviews per development line come from the pupil record system ({OTHER}) instead of being compiled in a spreadsheet. A bounded step drafts the revised programme text from the team's agreed changes; code checks every objective maps to a core goal code, and the teacher edits. Once the team has approved the programme, it is published to staff on the school's shared page. Team meetings and the decisions stay with the teachers and management.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evaluation data were compiled by hand and programme texts rewritten from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems produce group overviews; language models draft text from agreed changes.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing changes in a team takes time no tool shortens.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing a colleague's good idea into the programme for everyone.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafts and reads overviews instead of compiling them.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference.
Drafting programme texts is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from the current programme to the programme shared; the school plan is outside.
Input contract: core goals as a fixed list; group overviews from the pupil record; fallback is writing by hand.
Team meetings do not change.
No pupil names go into the drafting step.
s3 keeps 75 because the teacher reads and rewrites the draft for meaning; s5 keeps 20 for publishing.
research_questions: How much of the drafted text does the team change?

already_counted.description: Kindergarten teacher edits and approves the drafted programme text.

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher keeps the core goal list current.

approvals.approved_version: The revised programme exactly as checked with the team in s4, published once to all staff on the school's shared page; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small revisions each year, so the draft saves little and s3 keeps 90 (17.5); high: a full programme rewrite with drafts as designed (21.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare small tasks and assignments, administer them one to one or in groups, score them, check the scores, save them to the pupil record, and review group results.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher prepares tests and assignments to evaluate children's progress
Kindergarten teacher administers the tasks one to one or in small groups
Kindergarten teacher grades the tasks: on paper score forms today, on a tablet form that totals the scores after the change
Kindergarten teacher checks the scores
Kindergarten teacher types the scores into the pupil record: by hand today; after the change the tablet form saves them and the teacher confirms the save
Kindergarten teacher reviews group results to plan next steps

tasks.design: Assessment tasks come from a shared task bank per development line. The teacher scores on a tablet form, code totals the scores, and once the teacher has checked them the teacher saves them to the pupil record ({OTHER}), an ordinary save that needs no approval; the record shows a group overview. No software scores the children; the teacher's judgement sets every score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tasks were prepared fresh, scored on paper and typed into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records take tablet scores and show group overviews.
tasks.still_hard: Young children's performance varies with the day.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a child knows the answer but is too shy to say it.

reach.learn: Whether group overviews show needs sooner.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records with learning-goal tracking.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3, so no software scores children here.

assumptions: Boundary: from the development lines to next steps; formal reports to parents are outside.
Input contract: task bank kept by the kindergarten team; fallback is paper forms.
Administering tasks and judging scores do not change.
Children's time does not change.
Scoring is a first record: s3 keeps 80, saving only the totalling. s5 keeps 20 for confirming the save; typing is gone.
research_questions: Do scores reach the record the same day?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher adds new tasks to the bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the task bank covers few development lines and group tasks stay on paper, so s1 keeps 80 and s5 keeps 60 (12.0); high: tablet forms and the bank used as designed (18.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet colleagues to plan lessons, check the plan against curriculum goals, build the lesson schedule for the period, check it, and share it with colleagues.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher confers with other staff members to plan lessons following approved curricula
Kindergarten teacher checks the plan against the approved curriculum goals
Kindergarten teacher schedules lessons for the period in a spreadsheet
Kindergarten teacher checks the lesson schedule
Kindergarten teacher e-mails the schedule to colleagues: gone after the change, because colleagues read it on the shared page

tasks.design: The planning page links each lesson to curriculum goal codes and shows goals not yet covered this period, so coverage is not checked by hand. A schedule template places fixed blocks such as gym hall times and holidays from the school calendar ({CALENDAR}); the teacher fills in the rest. Colleagues read the checked schedule on the shared page, so it is no longer e-mailed; saving it there is an ordinary save and needs no approval. Planning with colleagues stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Goal coverage was checked by hand and schedules built from scratch in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning tools link lessons to goal codes and place fixed blocks from the calendar.
tasks.still_hard: Sickness and events change the schedule every week.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with a colleague who teaches what, so both play to strengths.

evidence.claim: Planning tools can link lessons to curriculum goal codes and show uncovered goals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the curriculum to the schedule shared; the yearly timetable is outside.
Input contract: curriculum goal codes from the school; fixed blocks from the school calendar; fallback is a spreadsheet.
Planning with colleagues does not change.
Colleagues' time does not change.
s3 keeps 70: the template places only fixed blocks such as gym times and holidays; ordering the lessons stays with the teacher.

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher tags lessons with goal codes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stable schedules with few changes and lessons not tagged consistently, so s2 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 85 (12.2); high: several staff and frequent changes, as designed (20.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare lesson content, set up the classroom, write up the preparation for the supervisor, check the preparation file, and give the supervisor access.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher prepares lesson content for assigned classes

loop.input: The week plan, the lesson goal codes and the team's activity library.
loop.output: Draft lesson notes with goal, steps and materials.
loop.check: Code checks each lesson's goal code exists in the curriculum list and materials come from the library list; the teacher reads each drafted lesson against the week plan and the goal's meaning and rewrites what does not fit the class.
loop.stop: Stops when the teacher approves, or after two redrafts the teacher writes the notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each lesson needs its own steps; a template only gives the headings.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher prepares the classroom and materials
Kindergarten teacher writes up written evidence of preparation in the class folder
Kindergarten teacher checks the preparation file before the supervisor's visit
Kindergarten teacher gives the supervisor access to the checked file: by handing over the class folder today, by sharing it in the document space after the change

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts lesson notes from the week plan, goal codes and the team's activity library; code checks goals and materials, and the teacher edits. The approved notes in the document space ({DOCS}) are the written evidence of preparation, so no separate write-up is needed. Once the teacher has checked the file, the supervisor gets access to it. Preparing the classroom stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lessons were prepared from scratch and written up again for the class folder.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft lesson notes from goals; shared document spaces replace class folders.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted lessons can miss what this group of children needs.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing an activity because one child needs a win today.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits lesson drafts instead of writing and copying them.

reach.learn: Whether files are complete without reminders.

evidence.claim: Snappet uses AI to draft a class activity for a lesson goal.
With Oak's Aila, 464 primary teachers cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but it covered 7% of lessons and use declined over ten weeks.

assumptions: Boundary: from the week plan to the file with the supervisor; the supervisor's review is outside.
Input contract: goal codes from the school; activity library kept by the team; fallback is writing by hand.
Preparing the classroom does not change.
No pupil names go into the drafting step.
s1 keeps 75 because the teacher reads and rewrites the drafted notes for each class; s5 keeps 20 for sharing the file.
research_questions: Does use of lesson drafts last beyond the first weeks?

already_counted.description: Kindergarten teacher edits and approves drafted lesson notes.

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher keeps the activity library tagged with goal codes.

approvals.approved_version: The preparation file exactly as checked by the teacher in s4, shared once with the supervisor in the document space; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts are used for few lessons and the supervisor still wants a separate write-up, so s1 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 60 (15.0); high: drafts used for most lessons (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The kindergarten teacher keeps team decisions, assessing children, planning with colleagues and preparing the classroom; compiling data, retyping scores, hand-built schedules and duplicate write-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time to observe and respond to each child.
